owner_brief:
You are Marcus Bell, CFO of Tallowbird Software, a B2B SaaS company with about 300 customers. You own finance_model.xlsx, a monthly operating model from January 2026 to December 2028 that you built with Priya Shah, a finance analyst who left in June 2026.

Structure: Inputs, Revenue, P&L, Cash Flow and Balance Sheet tabs; row labels in column A, one column per month.

Inputs: Growth (4%) is month over month MRR growth, applied to beginning MRR each month. It is monthly, not annual; people misread it all the time. Monthly churn is 1.5% of beginning MRR. ARPA is $650 a month, CAC $5,200 per new customer. Starting MRR ($185,000) is left over from the first version; nothing uses it anymore because January 2026 is an actual. The headcount plan was approved by the board in July 2026. Costs per head are fully loaded monthly costs. AR is one month of revenue because customers pay net 30; AP is half of monthly costs.

Actuals: January to August 2026 are actuals from the monthly close, typed in as values. September 2026 onward are formulas. Actual revenue includes a little services revenue, so it does not tie exactly to MRR; forecast revenue is Ending MRR.

Known problems: May 2027 cash on the Balance Sheet is a typed number. Priya typed a rounded figure while testing a scenario and never put the link back, which is why the balance check is off that month. January 2027 revenue on the P&L has *1.07 in the formula; that was Priya's test of a 7% price increase, never approved, and it should come out. New MRR in November 2027 points at churn instead of Growth (copy and paste error). G&A in March 2028 is missing the fixed G&A. AR in July 2028 points at June's revenue. All of those are errors you want fixed.

Financing: a $15 million Series B is planned for March 2027 and typed into the Cash Flow tab. It is not closed yet.

Your goal: get the model clean before it goes to the board and investors in October, and answer the runway question with confidence.

You do not remember exact cell values; you would have to look. Answer only what you are asked, briefly, like a busy CFO. If a question is not covered here, say "not sure".

eval_questions.q: In which month is the balance check not zero, by how much, and why?
eval_questions.a: May 2027 only (Balance Sheet!R18 = 26,110.52): Total Assets exceed Total Liabilities & Equity because Cash in Balance Sheet!R4 is a typed number instead of the Cash Flow link.

eval_questions.q: What does the Growth input mean?
eval_questions.a: Month over month growth of MRR: each forecast month adds Growth x beginning MRR as New MRR (4% per month, not per year).

eval_questions.q: Which months are actuals and which are forecast?
eval_questions.a: Jan 2026 to Aug 2026 are actuals typed in as values (8 months); Sep 2026 onward are formulas.

eval_questions.q: Which formula cells break their row's pattern (ignore the first month and any formula with a typed number in it)?
eval_questions.a: Balance Sheet!AF5; P&L!AB9; Revenue!X5. New MRR in Nov 2027 multiplies by churn instead of Growth, G&A in Mar 2028 drops the fixed G&A, and AR in Jul 2028 points at the prior month's revenue.

eval_questions.q: Which formula has a typed number inside it, and how much revenue does it add in that month?
eval_questions.a: P&L!N4 is =Revenue!N7*1.07: a 7% uplift typed into the Jan 2027 revenue formula, adding $17,967.94 over Ending MRR.

eval_questions.q: What is Ending MRR in December 2028 as the model stands?
If New MRR followed its row's pattern in every forecast month, what would Ending MRR be in December 2028?
eval_questions.a: $452,948.82, versus $441,901.29 as built. The single wrong cell in Nov 2027 compounds through every later month.

eval_questions.q: What is Ending Cash in December 2028 on the Cash Flow tab?
What is total 2027 revenue on the P&L?
What is total 2027 net income on the P&L?
Which scalar input on the Inputs tab is not used by any formula?
eval_questions.a: Inputs!B3 (Starting MRR). Nothing references it; January 2026 Beginning MRR is typed as an actual instead.

eval_questions.a: $934,948.55 in Feb 2027, the month before the planned Series B lands.
